entities.summary:
Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Nahawandi, also called al-Nahawandi, was an 8th/9th century Persian astronomer born in the region of Khorasan, Persia (modern-day Iran and Afghanistan), who made significant contributions to the field of astronomy, particularly in the study of planetary motion and the development of a new astronomical table. His work, which included a commentary on the works of ancient Greek astronomers, had a lasting impact on the development of astronomy in the Islamic Golden Age. Al-Nahawandi's observations and calculations helped to refine our understanding of the solar system and laid the groundwork for later astronomical discoveries.


Al-Nahawandi was a prolific astronomer who worked under the patronage of the Abbasid Caliphate, producing a number of astronomical tables and commentaries that were widely disseminated throughout the Islamic world. His work was particularly influential in the development of Islamic astronomy, which played a significant role in the transmission of ancient Greek knowledge to Europe during the Middle Ages.


Despite his significant contributions to astronomy, little is known about al-Nahawandi's personal life, and his exact dates of birth and death are not certain. However, his work has had a lasting impact on the field of astronomy, and he remains an important figure in the history of Islamic science.
